Parking the roadmap. Stage 1 is complete and Stage 2 never started, so it parks as **1 of 2 stages complete**. Four deferred items will go to the backlog: unticked Stage 2, plus O2, O3 and O4 from Track A's Ranked list. Nothing else retires with it, because this roadmap had no spec and no methodology or critique files.

First I need the deferred-item schema and the current backlog, so the new entries match:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md   (Deferred-item schema)
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                          (may not exist yet)
```

Then I'll append this section to `specs/deferred_items.md`, fitted to the exact schema:

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices for boat operators (was Stage 2, Track B)
      Email boat operators within an hour of a new closure entry in the
      closure log's live feed. Parked unstarted when the canal study's
      funding ended.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll every 10 minutes)
      Done when: a notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a
      test an email reaches every listed address within an hour of a new
      closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was O2, Track A Ranked list #1)
      Turn the river-level forecast into a 7-day closure-risk outlook for
      each lock, using Stage 1's response curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md:
      under 2% of days below 3.1 m, about 60% at 3.8 m).
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop)
      Done when: each lock has a 7-day closure-risk outlook produced from the
      real river-level forecast, and the run's measured cost is recorded.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves, pooled across locks (was O3, Track A Ranked list #2)
      Fit a separate closure curve for each of the 14 locks, pooled across
      locks. Stage 1 found the four longest-record locks share nearly the
      same curve, so the gain from per-lock curves is open.
      Size: medium (about 14× Stage 1's 1.8 GB data volume)
      Done when: all 14 locks have a fitted curve on real data, and the
      run's measured cost is recorded.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was O4, Track A Ranked list #3)
      A static map page showing each lock's closure history.
      Size: small (about a day of work)
      Done when: boat operators can open a map page showing closure history
      for every lock.
```

Then I'll retire the roadmap:

```
mkdir -p specs/completed
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Edit specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md — add under the title:
    > PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Remaining stage and
    > Track A's Ranked list moved to specs/deferred_items.md
    > (## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06). Reason: canal study funding ended.
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: 1 of 2 stages complete; remaining work deferred"
```

Some things stay as they are:

- **Stage 1's findings file** (`specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`) stays in `specs/`, because the deferred O2 and O3 items point to it.
- **Text-message notices** are not parked. Stage 2's `Leaves out` said no stage or list item picks them up, so there is nothing to carry forward.

If any of these edits or the commit fails, I'll tell you what happened rather than report the roadmap as parked. Once it's done, nothing is waiting to be handed off. The four items will age in the backlog like any other deferred work.
